name: Critical Thinking
description: Holds an answer to the evidence behind it and reports each claim the evidence does not support. Today the claim it checks is a link: every link in the answer must be in the evidence.
purpose: Check every answer and plan against its measure before it reaches a person.
approach: Name the problem, ideal and metric of each request, check the result against them, and retry when it falls short.
milestones: 1. The evidence check runs on written answers with and without supporting links. 2. A second arm exists beside it. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Share of unsupported links in written answers that are reported, with no supported link reported.
outputs: The findings, one per claim the evidence does not support (an empty list when the answer held).
usage_notes: Pass the answer and the evidence text: critique(answer, evidence).

name: Subconscious
description: Finds and prepares information for the Mind. Keeps what a person knows as cards and recalls the ones that bear on the task at hand, from the asker's own scope: the cards a context assembler names for the query, then the cards the store finds by its words.
purpose: Give an AI the context a task needs and nothing from another person's scope.
approach: Store knowledge as cards and admit it by relevance within the scope of the asker.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-remember-and-recall chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Right context admitted, nothing from another scope.
outputs: The cards a task needs, in one rendered view with their ids.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Context Assembler
description: Selects the context a task needs from a store and renders it into one view, together with the ids of the cards it drew on.
purpose: Find the passages that bear on a request, for any consumer that keeps knowledge to draw on.
approach: Rank stored documents against the request by keywords, meaning or both, and return the top results.
milestones: BM25, vector, hybrid and composite arms with recorded runs on public retrieval sets.
knowledge: Retrieval quality depends on the corpus, so arms are compared on the same public and written queries.
measures_of_success: A relevant document is among the first five results.
parameters: The store and optional model provider the arm is built with, and the number of hits.
outputs: An assembled context view and the ids of the cards it drew on; it never raises.
usage_notes: Pass root= for the folder to index. With no root the corpus is empty and nothing is returned.

name: Context Retriever
description: Cuts a corpus of files into units at natural boundaries and returns, for a request, the units that answer it best first within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context.
purpose: Show a task the context it needs and little else, for any consumer that keeps its knowledge in files.
approach: A fielded keyword index and a local meaning index fused by rank, a reranker over the best candidates that also reads the import graph and the history of changes, and a confidence gate that returns nothing when the corpus does not answer; every arm is scored on one balanced number.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (cards-from-files), storing them (card-store) and rendering a view for a consumer's loop (context-assembler, whose file_retrieval arm reads this seat).
milestones: Lexical, latent, dense, fused, reranked, learned and abstaining arms recorded on one number over file, topic, orientation and no-context requests; a model reranker prepared for a recorded cassette.
knowledge: Retrieval papers favour hybrid first stages and rerankers; code retrieval gains from structure (names, imports, co-change); a consumer's own labelled history is the best training data and stays with the consumer.
measures_of_success: The balanced score of metric-retrieve-context, which counts the recall of needed files within the budget, graded nDCG, the noise tokens shown, the size of the index, cost and time.
parameters: The budget in tokens, the corpus (a mapping of path to text) and an optional history of past changes; each arm's own settings are constructor arguments.
inputs: A request in words, and the files to retrieve from the first time.
outputs: Hits: unit id, file, first line, score, tokens and text, best first; an empty list means no context is needed.
effects: Reads the corpus it is given and keeps an index and a vector cache in the folder it is given; no network, and no model unless the arm is a model reranker.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("retrieve-context", {"query": "where is the retry delay computed?", "files": {"net.py": "def retry_delay(attempt): ..."}})` returns the hits.

name: Mind
description: What the planning and responding AI can see for one request and how it outputs plans, requests and communications. Asks a model for the answer to a prompt at a tier, using the model the tier chooser measured best for that tier. Planning and streaming live in the consumer. The Mind has one intake with two sources, what the Subconscious prepares from the system's internal context and what the World brings in through Science and Tools, and the Assembler wires both to it.
purpose: Reason to a good answer at the lowest cost that still passes, for any product that needs an AI that plans and answers.
approach: Plan the steps, call the cheapest model tier that passes, and stream progress while the work runs.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-reason-and-answer has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-reason-and-answer has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-reason-and-answer chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer quality per dollar and per second.
parameters: A model-call seat and a tier-selection seat (built on first use, so a prompt with no tier never asks for it).
outputs: The text a model answers to the prompt at that tier.
effects: One model call per request, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: No arm yet: specified; implemented in Quest AI Runner, moving here.

name: Higher Mind
description: The long view across requests: long-term memory of what happened, long-term context that stays true across requests, and objectives that persist until they are met.
purpose: Keep the AI working toward what matters beyond the request in front of it.
approach: Hold long-term memory, long-term context and objectives as separate parts, each readable by the Mind.
milestones: 1. The long view survives from one request to the next (metric-higher-mind).
measures_of_success: The long view survives from one request to the next.
outputs: What the AI remembers, what it knows and what it is working toward.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Long-Term Memory
description: What happened across requests, kept so a later request can use it.
purpose: Let the AI remember across requests.
approach: Keep dated records of what happened and recall them by relevance and recency.
milestones: 1. A later request can use what an earlier one learned (metric-long-term-memory).
measures_of_success: A later request can use what an earlier one learned.
outputs: Remembered events that bear on a request.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Long-Term Context
description: What stays true across requests about a person, a team and their work, kept so each request starts from it.
purpose: Let each request start from what is already known.
approach: Keep standing facts apart from events and refresh them when they change.
milestones: 1. A request starts from the standing facts that bear on it (metric-long-term-context).
measures_of_success: A request starts from the standing facts that bear on it.
outputs: Standing facts that bear on a request.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Objectives
description: What the AI is working toward, kept until it is met, so work continues between requests.
purpose: Let the AI keep working toward a goal over many requests.
approach: Record each objective with its done-standard and check progress against it.
milestones: 1. An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard (metric-hold-objectives).
measures_of_success: An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard.
outputs: The objectives in progress and their state.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Intuition
description: What comes to mind for a request without being asked for: cards and facts the Subconscious offers because they are close to the request.
approach: Offer the closest items to a request, within a budget, and let the Mind take or ignore them.
milestones: 1. An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept (metric-offer-intuition).
measures_of_success: An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept.
outputs: Items offered to the Mind for a request.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.
